summary: Execute Coulomb solver color ranges with native parameters and shared-body ordering; validate contact coefficients directly.
regressions: 28 live Rust cases cover empty and tile/workgroup-boundary ranges, interleaved batches, shared bodies across colors, runtime bias modes, unknown mode values, cached writes and repeated ordered color programs.
Ten coefficient profiles cover zero timestep/frequency, differing static softness, length scales, the Nexus MAX_FLT sentinel and adjacent f32 values.
Dynamic bucket indices reproduced malformed Metal from a guarded buffer load inside a mutable scalar initializer; materializing the load first compiles and executes with unchanged arithmetic.
Empty ranges eliminate unreachable point code before interval analysis to avoid an unsigned-subtraction compiler failure.
Repeated fixture exports preserve generated replay artifacts and reproduce identical inputs and expected outputs; a second export previously failed when the destination directory already existed.
differences: No Rust physics change. Native solver uniforms are loaded by generated kernels, with MAX_FLT and TWO_PI bits derived from the live Rust exporter. Nexus MAX_FLT is 1e18, not IEEE f32::MAX.
The existing prepared-color pilot remains available; native-color adapters mirror the same Rust entry-point names and files.

The ordered program is a contact-iteration schedule over prepared tiles, not a complete simulation frame. Static sharing within a color, collision detection, joints, fused/tail optimizations and scene validation remain.

CPU/Metal and offline Ascend source validation are separate; hardware execution is not inferred from source output. Floating tolerances of the existing solve contract and its numerical boundary release block remain unchanged.
